name: Canned meats (with tin flag)
anchor: per-commodity sovereign metallic-contamination schedules for terrestrial animal foods — Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (the only credible instrument on the register with a complete meat, poultry and egg panel), EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 for cadmium in muscle meat, and FSANZ Schedule 19 for lead in muscle meat; canned forms additionally carry the canned-foods tin maximum level, and the plant-protein analogue row reads across from EU and Hong Kong pulse, soy and cereal commodity maximum levels
native_basis_label: as sold, whole can contents as packed (wet weight), including any jelly, brine or sauce consumed with the product; no drained-weight adjustment and no invented conversion factor, and because whole-contents application is the looser treatment relative to applying the muscle-meat maximum level to the meat fraction, certification additionally requires documented raw-material compliance against the same named component maximum levels
scope_note: Meat and poultry products hermetically sealed in a metal can and retort-processed: canned corned beef, canned luncheon meat and spiced ham, canned chicken and turkey, canned stewed and braised meat, canned meat pate and spread, and canned pet-food-adjacent human-grade meat. Canned fish and shellfish route to Category 6; canned soups, stews and complete meals whose meat content is one component among many route to Category 35; canned pet food routes to Category 17. THE TIN FLAG IS THIS ROW'S REASON TO EXIST: tin migrates from the internal surface of an unlacquered or damaged tinplate can into the food, so the canned-foods tin maximum level applies to this row and to no other row in Category 11.
basis_guard: (wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed|as sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part|fresh weight)
basis_guard_note: Category 11 is a dietary as-sold wet-weight category. The guard admits only register rows whose basis is a food-matrix content basis (wet weight, portion ordinarily consumed, product as placed on market, commodity, edible part, food as listed in the Cap 132V schedule). It rejects, by construction, food-contact specific-migration limits, toy and article element-migration limits, animal-feed 12%-moisture bases, dry-matter fertiliser limits, colour-additive ingredient purity specifications, and drinking-water statutory limits. A migration or purity-specification number is not a maximum level for a food and must never anchor a meat, poultry, or egg row.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only initial setting: the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact product form in its native basis; disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; control where neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.label: strictest applicable principal-component muscle-meat lead maximum level; all three candidate components sit at 100 ug/kg

stricter_unselected.basis: food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule; source unit mg/kg
stricter_unselected.scope: Canned chestnuts and canned chestnuts puree

Pb.substantiation: A canned meat product is not a separately named commodity in any credible sovereign contaminant instrument, so the exact cell is unregulated and the ceiling is a disclosed read-across from the maximum levels governing its principal components — the muscle meat of the species it is formulated from. All three credible candidate rows (Hong Kong Cap. 132V meat of cattle/pig/goat/sheep, Hong Kong meat of poultry, FSANZ Schedule 19 multi-species muscle meat excluding offal) sit at 0.1 mg/kg, so the binding value is 100 ug/kg regardless of species mix. BASIS TREATMENT, DISCLOSED IN THE DIRECTION IT ACTUALLY CUTS: the ceiling is applied to the FINISHED product as sold, in the same wet-weight basis the component maximum levels are written in, with no invented conversion factor. Applying a ceiling to the finished product rather than to its meat fraction is the LOOSER of the two available treatments, because a formulation that is part water, starch, rusk and brine can carry a higher concentration in its meat fraction than the muscle-meat maximum level itself allows. The programme does not paper over that with a claim of conservatism it has not earned; it closes the gap with a second, independent test. The meat raw material entering the formulation IS "meat of cattle, pig, goat and sheep" or "meat of poultry" within the meaning of the sovereign instruments, so those maximum levels apply to it as a commodity in their own right: every certified lot must document raw-material compliance against the named component maximum levels IN ADDITION to finished-product compliance against this ceiling, and neither test substitutes for the other. Mechanically separated meat and any lot containing edible offal (liver sausage, blood sausage, pate) is additionally screened against the sovereign offal maximum levels, which govern that ingredient but never loosen this row. BASIS OF THE BINDING INSTRUMENT, DISCLOSED: the two concurring instruments are written on DIFFERENT bases. FSANZ Schedule 19 states its maximum level for the portion ordinarily consumed (an as-consumed basis); Hong Kong Cap. 132V states the identical 0.1 mg/kg as-sold, for the edible portion after removal of bones and fat (Cap. 132V Part 2 Note 1). Because this row publishes an as-sold ceiling, the Hong Kong as-sold row is named as the binding instrument and the FSANZ row is disclosed as an independent sovereign value concurring at the same number. The published ceiling therefore rests on an instrument written in this row's own basis, and no as-consumed value is relabelled as-sold. The number is unaffected: both instruments sit at 100 ug/kg, so the strictest-applicable selection is identical either way. AUDIT DISPOSITION — hk_cap132v_pb_canned-chestnuts-and-canned-chestnuts-puree_50 (0.05 mg/kg, Hong Kong): this row surfaces in the audit scan only because this subcategory's scope regex matches the word 'canned', and it is REVIEWED AND DECLINED. It is a commodity maximum level for canned chestnuts and chestnut puree, a tree-nut food. 'Canned' names a packaging format shared with this row, not a shared product scope; a lead ceiling for a canned nut does not govern canned meat any more than the canned-fruit or canned-vegetable rows in the same instrument do. Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets no canned-meat lead maximum level, which is precisely why this row is a component read-across from the muscle-meat rows rather than a direct government lookup.

Cd.label: strictest applicable principal-component muscle-meat cadmium maximum level; both candidate components sit at 50 ug/kg
Cd.substantiation: The cadmium ceiling for canned meat reads across from the muscle-meat cadmium maximum levels of its principal components: EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 for bovine, sheep, pig and poultry meat and Hong Kong Cap. 132V for poultry meat, both 0.05 mg/kg. Applied to the finished product as sold with no invented conversion factor, and paired with the same mandatory raw-material test described in the lead cell, because finished-product application alone is the looser treatment. Offal-containing formulations (liver sausage, pate) carry a cadmium-accumulating ingredient and are flagged for the offal maximum levels as an additional test, not as a licence to raise this row.

tAs.label: strictest applicable principal-component total-arsenic maximum level (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, 500 ug/kg for both meat of animal and meat of poultry)
tAs.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a total-arsenic maximum level for terrestrial animal meat, at 0.5 mg/kg for both meat of animal and meat of poultry. A canned meat product reads across from those principal-component values at face value on the finished product.

iAs.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for canned meat. Every credible inorganic-arsenic instrument on the register is scoped elsewhere: EU 2023/915 and EU 2025/1891 to rice, rice products, fruit juices, infant food and seafood; UK, Health Canada and US FDA to rice-based and juice matrices; Hong Kong Cap. 132V to rice and aquatic animals. A NOT-MATERIAL determination is deliberately REJECTED for this cell rather than adopted for convenience: organoarsenical feed additives (roxarsone, nitarsone, arsanilic acid, carbarsone) were lawfully administered to poultry and swine in major producing markets within living memory and are documented to leave arsenic residues in edible tissue, so the programme will not make the affirmative claim that no inorganic-arsenic pathway exists in terrestrial animal food. For the ruminant rows, where no equivalent additive history applies, the absence of that pathway does not by itself substantiate a not-material determination either, because neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists for the cell in any case. Because no sovereign number governs the cell and no near-neighbour cell is a supportable analogue (a rice or seafood inorganic-arsenic maximum level describes a different contamination mechanism entirely), the cell is a control: testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
iAs.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS speciation. Speciation is reflex-triggered on every lot whose total-arsenic screen is quantifiable above the method limit of quantitation, and unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier, slaughter establishment, or country of origin. Any quantifiable inorganic arsenic is escalated to the certification committee together with the feed-additive and origin declaration; the lot cannot be released on an inorganic-arsenic result while the escalation is open, and a total-arsenic result at or above the binding total-arsenic maximum level is a hard stop irrespective of speciation.

tHg.label: strictest applicable principal-component total-mercury maximum level (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, 50 ug/kg for both meat of animal and meat of poultry)
tHg.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 0.05 mg/kg total mercury for both meat of animal and meat of poultry; canned meat reads across from those principal-component values at face value. A formulation incorporating fish, fish protein or a marine-derived ingredient is re-routed for the Category 6 seafood mercury ceilings, and the stricter applicable value binds.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. A canned meat product carries no methylation pathway and no aquatic trophic transfer, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), so it is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury cell (50 ug/kg total mercury, Hong Kong Cap. 132V). No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling and none is set by any credible sovereign government for this product form.
MeHg.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell; methylmercury speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total-mercury result approaches the binding total-mercury maximum level, or where the formulation incorporates a fish, fish-meal, or marine-derived ingredient, which would additionally route the lot to the Category 6 seafood mercury ceilings.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury content limit for meat, poultry, game, eggs, or meat analogues. The credible methylmercury instruments (EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, FSANZ Schedule 19, Hong Kong Cap. 132V) are scoped exclusively to fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic animals. Methylmercury is a species of, and arithmetically bounded by, total mercury.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I); UK retained contaminants law; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (CPG 540.600); FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations Part 2 Schedule — none sets a methylmercury limit for a terrestrial animal food, an egg, or a plant-protein meat analogue.

Ni.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for canned meat. The EU nickel maximum levels recorded on the register (the eu2024_ni_* family) are drawn exclusively over plant matrices — cereals, pulses, legume, leafy and root vegetables, tree nuts, oilseeds, cocoa — and the only other credible nickel values are drinking-water statutory limits and a food-contact specific-migration limit, both in bases that cannot govern the content of a food. A plant-commodity nickel maximum level is not a supportable near-neighbour for animal muscle tissue, which accumulates nickel by a different route and at a different order of magnitude, so no read-across is available and no ceiling is invented.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU and per production line. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit, or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to nickel-bearing stainless contact surfaces (grinders, mincers, brine injectors, forming plates). No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

Sn.basis: as sold, whole can contents as packed (wet weight)
Sn.label: strictest applicable sovereign canned-food tin maximum level; EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 binds at 200000 ug/kg (200 mg/kg) against 250 mg/kg in Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19 and Hong Kong Cap. 132V
Sn.substantiation: Four credible sovereign instruments regulate tin in canned food other than canned beverages: EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 at 200 mg/kg, Codex CXS 193-1995 at 250 mg/kg, FSANZ Schedule 19 at 250 mg/kg, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V at 250 mg/kg. All four are named so the selection is auditable, and the strictest applicable value binds: 200 mg/kg = 200000 ug/kg. The canned-BEVERAGE tin maximum levels (EU 100 mg/kg, Hong Kong 150 mg/kg) are stricter but are a different product form and are not applicable to a canned meat; the canned infant-food and canned-infant-formula tin maximum levels (50 mg/kg, EU and UK) are stricter still but are infant scopes, and products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule. The superseded pre-2019 Hong Kong all-food entry is gated out by its register status.

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium maximum level for meat, poultry, game or eggs. The credible aluminium values on the register are drinking- and bottled-water statutory limits (EU 2020/2184, US FDA 21 CFR 165.110, Health Canada), a food-contact specific-migration limit (EU 10/2011), toy element-migration limits, and the FSANZ Schedule 19 aluminium maximum levels for infant formula. None can anchor this row: the water and migration values are in a different basis, and an adult food must not borrow an infant-formula maximum level (products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule). No read-across is supportable and no ceiling is invented.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to aluminium contact surfaces and packaging (foil, trays, aluminium cookware, aluminium-containing processing aids). No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium in food is dominated by benign trivalent chromium, an essential trace element; the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, which does not persist in this matrix (see the Cr-VI cell). The Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level is a real sovereign limit and is published here, but it is recorded as a SCREEN: it is a contact-surface and equipment-leaching tripwire, not a standalone protective ceiling, and it is excluded from the firm-limit count.
Cr.label: read-across from the Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level for meat of animal (1000 ug/kg), published as a screen; the meat-of-poultry entry in the same instrument carries the identical value
Cr.substantiation: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium maximum level for canned meat. The nearest applicable sovereign cells are Hong Kong Cap. 132V meat of animal and meat of poultry, both 1 mg/kg; the general animal row is named and the poultry row is disclosed at the same value. Published as a screen because total chromium is dominated by trivalent chromium and is not the health-relevant analyte; on this row the screen is specifically an equipment tripwire, since bowl choppers, emulsifiers, brine injectors and forming plates are stainless-steel contact surfaces.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in this matrix. A canned meat product is a wet, reducing, protein- and thiol-rich medium; Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by tissue reductants (cysteine, glutathione, ascorbate) and by the acid and heat of digestion and cooking, so a Cr(VI) figure reported on such a matrix is an artifact of the extraction chemistry of the total-chromium screen rather than a measurement of a species that persists in the food. The determination follows the same reference-method adjudication recorded for the hexavalent-chromium cell in the infant-formula category (data/workbench standards Cr-VI adjudication), applied here to an animal-tissue matrix. Hexavalent chromium is in any event a species of, and bounded by, the published total-chromium screen (Cr-VI <= total Cr). SCOPE OF THIS DETERMINATION — POULTRY CARVE-OUT: this not-material determination rests on the red-meat matrix evidence (saraiva2021, bovine meat) and is NOT extended to a poultry-containing formulation. Where the declared formulation contains poultry, the lot inherits the poultry-product row's hexavalent-chromium control in full, including the mandatory EN 15192 / EPA 6800 determination and the supplier feed-input declaration covering chrome-tanned leather and tannery-waste protein. See the poultry-product Cr-VI cell for the withdrawal record and the mahmud2011-crvi-chicken-pakistan pathway evidence behind it.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-chromium screen (Cr cell). Alkaline-extraction Cr(VI) determination (IC-ICP-MS) is reflex-triggered only where the total-chromium screen exceeds the published screen value, in which case the investigation is directed at stainless-steel contact surfaces, grinders, and brine or marinade equipment rather than at the raw material. Where the declared formulation contains poultry, the poultry-product row's hexavalent-chromium control applies to the lot in addition to this reference method, and Cr(VI) determination is mandatory rather than reflex-triggered.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food. Every credible Cr(VI) instrument on the register is an article, textile, leather, toy-migration, tattoo-ink, fertiliser or electrical-equipment limit in a non-food basis, and applying one to a food matrix would be a basis conflation the compiler's basis guard rejects. Total chromium is regulated for meat and poultry by Hong Kong Cap. 132V and is published here as a screen.
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915; Regulation (EU) 10/2011; Directive 2009/48/EC; REACH restrictions); UK; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA; FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule — none sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for food.
